How is West Virginia organized, and who handles my house sale paperwork?

West Virginia has 55 counties, and nearly every record tied to a house sale lives at the county level. Counties are not run by a single mayor or executive. The state constitution splits county government among seven separately elected offices: the county commission, county clerk, circuit clerk, sheriff, assessor, prosecuting attorney and surveyor of lands.

For a seller, three of those offices matter most. The assessor values the property, the sheriff is a good first call about what is owed, and the county clerk records the deed and handles probate. Our own state property tax guide walks through how assessment and billing fit together.

  • Assessor: ask about the value on file and any exemption already claimed.
  • Sheriff: ask what is owed on the parcel and whether anything is past due.
  • County clerk: ask about recording a deed, getting a copy of what is recorded, or opening an estate.
  • Circuit clerk and magistrate court: these handle court filings if a lien, lawsuit or eviction touches the property.

Offices, hours and fees differ from county to county, so a short phone call before listing or signing anything saves time. The county guides we list further down name the offices for each county we cover.

What does an as-is cash sale mean for a West Virginia homeowner?

An as-is cash sale means the buyer pays without a mortgage and takes the house in its current condition, so you do not paint, patch or replace anything first. That matters in a state where many homes are older and repair bills can eat into a sale price.

The paperwork still follows the normal path. A deed is signed and recorded with the county clerk, liens are paid from the proceeds, and a title company or attorney usually handles the closing. We have not confirmed a single statewide rule on who must run a closing, so ask the title company or your own attorney how it works in your county.

  • You skip the listing prep, showings and the wait for a buyer's lender.
  • You still owe any mortgage payoff, unpaid taxes and recorded liens.
  • You still deal with tenants, a probate case or co-owners if they apply to your house.

If you want to see how a sale could look for your address, we explain the process on our city pages for Charleston, Huntington, Morgantown, Parkersburg and Wheeling.

What transfer costs come with selling a house in West Virginia?

West Virginia charges an excise tax on transferring real estate, and the statute puts the rate at $1.10 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 shown on the deed. A second county tax of 55 cents per $500 applies as well, and a county commission may raise that county portion up to $1.65 per $500 by a majority vote after published notice.

Only one state tax and one county tax are paid on any one document, and the grantor, meaning the seller, pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without it being paid. Sales for consideration also carry a flat $20 fee collected by the county clerk before recording.

ItemWhat the statute says
Base transfer tax$1.10 per $500 of value or fraction
County transfer tax55 cents per $500, countywide increase allowed up to $1.65
Who usually paysThe grantor, unless the grantee accepts the deed unpaid
Housing fee$20 on a transfer for consideration
Who collectsCounty clerk, at recording

As a rough example, a $100,000 sale has 200 units of $500, so the $1.10 portion comes to $220 and the 55 cent portion to $110. Your county rate may differ, so confirm it with the clerk before you rely on a number.

How does foreclosure work in West Virginia?

West Virginia homes are usually financed with a deed of trust, and the lender enforces it through a trustee's sale at public auction rather than through a lawsuit. State law lets the trustee sell the property after a default, once the conditions written into the deed of trust have been met.

The notice rules are set out in the Code. The trustee publishes a notice of sale in the county where the house sits, and a copy goes to the borrower by certified mail at the address named in the deed of trust. A subordinate lienholder who has told the primary lienholder about its lien by certified mail gets its own notice at least twenty days before the sale.

  • The notice must list the time and place of sale, the parties, the deed date and recording book, a description of the land and the terms of sale.
  • A good faith buyer at the sale is not affected by defects in the notice to junior lienholders.

We did not find a fixed statewide count of days from first missed payment to auction, because it depends on the deed of trust terms. Read every letter you receive and talk to a West Virginia attorney about your own file.

What happens when I inherit a house in West Virginia?

You generally start at the county clerk's probate office in the county where the owner lived at death. Clerks qualify a person as executor or administrator, and that person gets a certificate showing authority to act for the estate.

One county clerk, Jefferson County, publishes its process online and it shows how this tends to work. Opening an estate typically costs between $80 and $100 there, and a will must be witnessed by two people. With no will and more than one heir, the person asking to serve waits thirty days unless every other heir signs a notarized consent. Bonding rules also apply. Other counties may differ slightly, so call yours.

  • Small estate affidavit: Jefferson County lists a limit of under $50,000 in personal property and no probate real estate, so a house usually means a regular estate.
  • Waiting period: thirty days with a will and sixty days without one, for the small estate route.
  • Attorney: not required by the clerk, though complicated estates may call for one.

For tax questions, we cover what heirs may owe in our estate and inheritance tax guide.

Does West Virginia offer a homestead exemption I should know about before selling?

Yes, but it is narrow. The first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner occupied home is exempt from property tax when the owner is 65 or older or certified permanently and totally disabled, and the owner has lived in West Virginia for the two calendar years before the tax year. Only one exemption is allowed per homestead.

The key point for sellers is what happens at transfer. The exemption attaches to the home as of the July 1 assessment date, and if the home passes by deed, will or otherwise, it comes off on the next July 1 unless the new owner qualifies on their own. A buyer should not count on inheriting your exemption. Details on filing are in our homestead exemption guide.

What if tenants live in the house I want to sell?

A signed lease does not vanish when a landlord sells. Under West Virginia law the buyer steps into the landlord's position, and a tenant can hold the new owner to the lease terms. The security deposit follows the property too, so whoever holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends must handle it.

If you need the house empty, an eviction starts with a verified petition filed in magistrate or circuit court in the county where the rental sits. Our guides on landlord and tenant law and eviction notice rules explain the timelines. If you also have an unwelcome occupant who is not a tenant, see our page on squatters and adverse possession.

Is radon a concern when selling an older West Virginia home?

It can be. The West Virginia Department of Health says radon is a gas released from rocks, soil and water that can build up inside homes, and the only way to know a home's level is to test. The EPA recommends action at 4 picoCuries per liter of air or higher, and the CDC states that radon reduction systems can cut levels by up to 99 percent.

The department has offered free test kits to residents. To ask for one, email radon@wv.gov or call 304-352-5039. A test result does not stop a cash sale, but a buyer may price in a mitigation system, so knowing your number helps. We left out flood, landslide and well and septic points because we could not confirm statewide figures from official pages, so ask your county health department and the assessor about those.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does West Virginia have?

West Virginia has 55 counties, and each one has its own clerk, assessor and sheriff, so records for your house sit in the county where it is located.

Is foreclosure in West Virginia handled by a court?

Most loans use a deed of trust, and the trustee sells the home at public auction after publishing notice in the county. The notice must also be mailed to the borrower by certified mail.

Who pays the transfer tax when I sell?

The statute says the grantor, the seller, pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without the tax paid. The rate is $1.10 per $500 plus a county portion.

Do I need probate to sell an inherited house?

Usually yes. Jefferson County lists its small estate route as limited to estates with no probate real estate, so a house normally means opening an estate at the county clerk.

Can I sell a house with tenants?

Yes. The lease continues with the buyer, who also takes on the deposit duties. Settle in writing who carries the deposit.

Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?

No. If the home passes by deed, the $20,000 exemption comes off on the next July 1 unless the new owner qualifies separately.

Where do I check my property tax bill?

Call the county sheriff or assessor. Our county guides list the offices for the counties we cover.

Do I have to repair the house before a cash sale?

No. An as-is sale means you sell in current condition, though liens, taxes and a mortgage payoff still come out of proceeds.
